form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Peters (for himself, Ms. Stabenow, Mrs. Gillibrand, and Ms. Cortez Masto) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

form.official-title: To make trade adjustment assistance available to workers whose jobs are eliminated through automation, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the TAA for Automation Act of 2019.

section.header: Eligibility of workers whose jobs are eliminated through automation for trade adjustment assistance

subsection.text: Section 222(a)(2) of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2272(a)(2)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (A)(iii), by striking ; or and inserting a semicolon; and
by adding at the end the following:

clause.text: there has been a shift in production of articles or supply of services by such workers’ firm from utilizing the workers to methods or systems primarily utilizing automation; and
the shift described in clause (i) contributed importantly to such workers' separation or threat of separation; or
the sales or production, or both, of such firm have decreased absolutely; and
the use of automation in the production of articles or services like or directly competitive with articles produced or services supplied by such firm has increased; and
the increase in the use of automation described in clause (ii) contributed importantly to such workers' separation or threat of separation and to the decline in the sales or production of such firm.

subsection.text: Section 222(c) of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2272(c)) is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating paragraphs (1) through (4) as paragraphs (2) through (5), respectively; and
by inserting before paragraph (2), as redesignated by paragraph (1), the following:
The term automation means using technology to produce a good or service previously produced by human work.

subsection.text: Section 222 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2272) is amended by adding at the end the following:

When the Secretary certifies a group of workers under this section as eligible to apply for adjustment assistance, the Secretary shall specify in the certification the basis for the eligibility of the group under subsection (a).

Subsections (b) and (c) of section 222 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2272) are amended by striking subsection (a) each place it appears and inserting subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (a)(2).
Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Labor shall—

paragraph.text: prescribe regulations to carry out the amendments made by this section; and

submit to Congress a report that includes recommendations for any changes to law necessary to carry out the amendments made by this section, including any changes to section 236(a)(2)(A) of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2296(a)(2)(A)).

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall—

paragraph.text: take effect on the date that is 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act; and
apply with respect to petitions for certifications of eligibility filed under section 221 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2271) on or after the date described in paragraph (1).

section.header: Workforce advisory board or subcommittee on automation

subsection.text: The Secretary of Labor shall establish an advisory board, or form a subcommittee of an advisory board that exists as of the date of the enactment of this Act, to provide recommendations to the Secretary on addressing the impact of automation on the workforce, including matters relating to jobs and occupations at risk of elimination as a result of automation.

In establishing the advisory board or subcommittee under subsection (a), the Secretary shall ensure that the advisory board or subcommittee consists of nationally representative members, including the balanced participation of—

paragraph.text: State boards, as defined in section 3 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (29 U.S.C. 3102);
nonprofit entities, or community-based organizations, with experience researching the impact of automation on the workforce;
academic experts in the field of workforce development, labor economics, and program evaluation;
engineering and technology experts, such as experts from the National Institute of Standards and Technology; and
any other stakeholders the Secretary considers appropriate.
Not less frequently than annually, the advisory board or subcommittee established under subsection (a) shall—

clause.text: occupations at risk of elimination as a result of automation; and
occupations experiencing above average decline for which there is evidence that technological advancement has contributed to that decline;

subparagraph.text: evaluate strategies for workforce development based on measurements of impact on the workforce due to automation and on other relevant evidence; and
provide recommendations to the Secretary and to Congress based on that evaluation.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall disseminate the strategies recommended under paragraph (1) to relevant stakeholders and make such strategies available to the public.

subsection.text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the advisory board or subcommittee established under subsection (a).
In this section, the term automation means using technology to produce a good or service previously produced by human work.
